_what_this_is: Pivota-authored Tier-G ingredient KB entry for Glycolic Acid (AHA) (ADR-002 v2-lite format). Evidence grade B. All 2 citation(s) verified to resolve on PubMed/PMC via web search at authoring 2026-07-08. consider_separating: BHA at the same step on sensitive skin

watchouts.what_to_do: Daily broad-spectrum SPF is essential; AHAs increase UV sensitivity for up to a week after use.
Start low and infrequent; avoid stacking with other strong acids or a retinoid at the same step.

benefits.mechanism: Glycolic acid reduces cohesion between corneocytes in the lower stratum corneum, accelerating desquamation and epidermal renewal; a pilot histologic study showed epidermal and dermal remodeling of photoaged skin (PMID 8642081).
benefits.what_it_means: Resurfaces dull, rough skin for visibly smoother, brighter texture over 4-8 weeks.

benefits.mechanism: Sustained AHA use is associated with epidermal thickening and increased dermal collagen and glycosaminoglycans in a double-blind vehicle-controlled trial of 8% glycolic/lactic creams (PMID 8651713).
benefits.what_it_means: Softens the look of fine lines and photodamage with consistent use.

benefits.mechanism: Faster desquamation disperses clustered surface pigment and smooths the stratum corneum.
benefits.what_it_means: Evens the look of tone and fades post-blemish marks by speeding surface turnover.

evidence.summary: Surface-renewal mechanism and dermal remodeling shown in controlled histologic and double-blind vehicle-controlled human trials; graded B.

citations.title: Effects of alpha-hydroxy acids on photoaged skin: a pilot clinical, histologic, and ultrastructural study
citations.source: Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology (Ditre, Van Scott et al.); PMID 8642081

citations.title: Topical 8% glycolic acid and 8% L-lactic acid creams for the treatment of photodamaged skin: a double-blind vehicle-controlled clinical trial
citations.source: Archives of Dermatology (Stiller et al.); PMID 8651713

overview: Glycolic acid resurfaces dull, rough skin by loosening dead cells at the skin surface, revealing smoother, brighter texture; with sustained use it is also associated with increased dermal collagen in controlled studies.

ingredient.what_it_is: The smallest alpha-hydroxy acid (AHA). Its small molecular size gives it the fastest penetration of the AHAs, making it the most-studied for surface renewal.

marketing_vs_reality.reality: At cosmetic strengths glycolic acid gently accelerates the skin’s natural exfoliation; it is not a chemical peel. Deeper resurfacing requires professional concentrations under supervision.
